topics.flagship-ru-ua: Repeated Russian airstrikes on a school serving as a humanitarian aid center in Zaporizhzhia region reportedly killed at least 26 people, including rescuers and police (4 outlets); Zelensky called the attack 'horrific'. Zelensky also said Ukrainian intelligence indicates Russia is preparing a new massive strike on energy and logistics infrastructure, possibly timed to the US midterms, and one report says Patriot interceptor supply is lagging despite 500 missiles on order. Other items include a multi-day ceasefire that let hundreds leave a Russian-occupied city, an FSB claim of booby-trapped headsets aimed at Russian drone operators, and rhetorical exchanges between Russian and UK/European officials.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Gulf states are reportedly bracing for a possible US attack on Iran after the US midterms (3 outlets). A single-outlet report citing Axios says Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike right after the midterms. Iran said on Nov. 2 it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US accepts its conditions, while an Iranian official said the 'ball is in the US court' as talks stall despite a June memorandum meant to end the war that began with US-Israeli strikes in February. Iranian officials also criticized the US over the NPT, and a statement attributed to Iran's supreme leader about responses having 'no geographical limits' prompted speculation about Europe. In Yemen, a Saudi-led coalition intercepted a missile amid fighting in al-Jawf, and Houthi-affiliated media reported seven wounded in strikes on Hodeidah (single source).
topics.T15: Flooding from a powerful storm triggered mandatory evacuations across the US Southwest, with some communities cut off as rivers surged (2 outlets). Japan launched a new disaster prevention agency and urged residents to stockpile food and water for up to seven days. Indonesia's BNPB issued rainy-season preparedness measures and a youth tsunami-awareness training was held; both are routine preparedness items.
topics.T01: Sudan has filed complaints with the UN against Ethiopia over one-way drone attacks that it says have killed or wounded 484 civilians since February (single source). Commentary notes renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia could hurt its economy. Politico reportedly says NATO fears Trump could reduce US involvement if Republicans lose the midterms. The remaining items are analysis or opinion, plus a South Korean soldier's death at a front-line unit that is under investigation.
topics.T02: Displaced Sudanese face a worsening aid situation and famine warnings. Separately, US sanctions are reported to be pushing Cuba's healthcare system toward crisis, affecting more than nine million people, with Washington and Havana blaming each other. Each item comes from a single outlet.
topics.T03: Coverage is limited to a single DW explainer on biological weapons, noting concern over biotech and AI developments. No specific bio/chem incident or event is reported.
topics.T04: An anthrax outbreak is killing hippos in DR Congo's Virunga National Park, with drought and conflict compounding the threat (2 outlets). Health officials warned an 'unprecedented' disease outbreak, mostly in Africa, is 'very dire' and that countries should increase preparedness (3 outlets). Madagascar imposed a 21-day quarantine and entry curbs on travelers from Kenya amid Ebola concerns, and Kenya was flagged as high risk for Rift Valley fever. One item is a stale 2020 coronavirus piece and should be disregarded.
topics.T05: Belgian PM Bart De Wever has reportedly handed in his resignation after budget talks failed, and the king is weighing whether to accept it (single source). In Poland, the dispute between PM Tusk and President Nawrocki over the Constitutional Tribunal continues. A single-outlet report describes a sweeping purge of China's military leadership under Xi; the other items are opinion pieces.
topics.T06: Rioting and looting in Frankfurt, which left about 100 officers injured, followed student protests over education and living costs (2 outlets), and German ministers vowed a tough response, with the interior minister blaming left-wing groups and migrant 'troublemakers'. French protest violence eased, though scattered riots hit Germany and further action is expected. An attempted-murder investigation was opened in Paris over a Molotov cocktail thrown at police. Spanish police arrested two alleged riot organizers in Málaga.
topics.T08: Troops in Kebbi, Nigeria, rescued 11 kidnap victims and stopped a terrorist ambush (2 outlets). In Ireland, Abdullah Khan was jailed for six and a half years over a stabbing of a garda and an arson attack. In Australia, the opposition criticized the release of a convicted terrorist linked to the alleged Bondi gunman. The DRC budget and Somalia-Türkiye items are not incident reports.
topics.T10: Russia is reportedly nearing completion of a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad capable of monitoring much of Europe, raising NATO concern. Other items: the US military is exploring commercial 5G networks for drone defense after trials in Latvia, South Korea is launching a new attack submarine, and Ethiopia announced it is acquiring Su-35 jets with S-400 systems to follow. More than 100,000 German students rallied against spending cuts and plans to revive conscription.
topics.T11: The Royal Navy intercepted a Russian spy ship off Scotland after it was caught closely monitoring NATO war games (3 outlets). US and Indian forces began the Tiger Triumph 2026 exercise in Visakhapatnam, and Indian and Sri Lankan navies held a joint exercise. The US Army is reportedly training soldiers to set up temporary mass burial sites for the first time since 1953 amid the Iran conflict, and British troops will join a drill preparing for a Ukraine peace deployment.
topics.T12: Russia and Ukraine each reported cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems, including fake nuclear warnings in Ukraine (13 outlets). Fridge-freezer hacks have hit more European grocery stores, with temperatures reportedly rising above 100 degrees (4 outlets). Security items include Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days chained in attacks since at least October 1, C3RB3R ransomware targeting Synology NAS devices, and over 1,000 unpatched GitLab servers. A Binance hack, a GMO Internet Group breach, and AI-assisted North Korean crypto theft were also reported.
topics.T13: Coverage is sparse and largely partisan. One outlet reports that more than 10,000 boat migrants have reached Britain since Andy Burnham became PM, and another is an opinion piece on European backlash over immigration.
topics.T14: Russia's FSB said it detained a teenager planning a terror attack on a major Moscow museum after a US tip-off (6 outlets). The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia issued a security alert to Americans over possible Houthi attacks (3 outlets). More than 300 people were arrested at a protest outside the US Embassy in London against the Palestine Action ban.
topics.T16: Rep. Haley Stevens' endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's Senate race drew backlash from Democratic allies (4 outlets). Lula's win in Brazil was covered, as was a Human Rights Watch accusation of a post-election crackdown on the opposition in Zambia. Iliana Yotova won Bulgaria's presidential election, and a poll shows a train tragedy hurting Spain's Socialists ahead of the Nov. 29 snap election. Other items concern US election-integrity disputes and an Israeli report on the Shin Bet chief.

bluf: Russia and Ukraine each reported cyberattacks on their emergency alert systems, and Ukraine saw fake nuclear warnings, in a story carried by 13 outlets while strikes continue in both countries. Russia's FSB announced the detention of a teenager allegedly planning a terror attack on a major Moscow museum after a US tip-off. Gulf states are reportedly bracing for a possible US attack on Iran after the US midterms, and a single-outlet report citing Axios says Netanyahu is pressing Trump to strike immediately afterward. Iran has said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US accepts its conditions, while talks remain stalled. In Yemen, a Saudi-led coalition reportedly intercepted a missile amid fighting in al-Jawf, and Houthi-affiliated media reported seven wounded in strikes on Hodeidah. An anthrax outbreak is killing hippos in DR Congo's Virunga National Park, with drought and conflict compounding the threat. Separately, repeated Russian airstrikes on a school used as an aid center in Zaporizhzhia reportedly killed at least 26 people, and Zelensky warns of a further massive strike on energy and logistics infrastructure. Belgian PM Bart De Wever has also reportedly resigned after budget talks failed, with the king yet to decide whether to accept it.
